children: Malaysian palm oil futures rose on Thursday, driven by firmer rival Dalian palm olein but sluggish export demand and soft Chicago soyoil capped the gains.
The benchmark palm oil contract (FCPOc3) for November delivery on the Bursa Malaysia Derivatives Exchange gained 24 ringgit, or 0.48%, to 4,982 ringgit ($1,233.17) a metric ton by the midday break.
"Crude palm oil futures traded higher as it was supported by a strong Dalian palm olein which rallied by more than a 100 yuan," a Kuala Lumpur-based trader said.

However, the absence of fresh destination buying, coupled with weakness in Chicago soyoil as well as the expectations of a surge in Malaysian palm oil August end-stocks limited gains, said Anilkumar Bagani, commodity research head at brokerage Sunvin Group.
Cargo surveyors estimated that exports of Malaysian palm oil products in August fell between 6.5% and 14.9% from a month earlier.
Dalian's most-active soyoil contract (DBYcv1) rose 0.96%, while its palm oil contract
added 0.85%. Soyoil prices on the Chicago Board of Trade (BOcv1) were down 0.62%.
Palm oil tracks the price movements of rival edible oils, as it competes for a share of the global vegetable oils market.
Oil prices edged lower as investors weighed the uncertainty of renewed military strikes between the U.S. and Iran that risk disrupting supplies from the Middle East.
Weaker crude oil futures make palm a less attractive option for biodiesel feedstock.
The ringgit, palm's currency of trade, strengthened 0.02% against the dollar, making the commodity slightly expensive for buyers holding foreign currencies.
Palm oil may revisit its August 21 high of 5,031 ringgit per metric ton, as it has almost recovered from a drop to the August 28 low of 4,799 ringgit, Reuters technical analyst Wang Tao said.
